parole.testo: From Hokkien 阿媽 /阿妈 (a-má, “paternal grandmother”). See also Hokkien 俺媽 /俺妈 (án-má), Portuguese Templo de A-Má.

parole.significato: Someone who is heavily tattooed.

parole.significato: A white person, especially one perceived as a foreigner rather than a local inhabitant.
parole.testo: Borrowed from Hokkien 紅毛／红毛 (âng-mô͘, “person of Western descent”, literally “red hair”).

parole.significato: Synonym of red envelope (“hongbao”).
parole.testo: From Hokkien 紅包／红包 (âng-pau, literally “red packet”). Doublet of hong bao.

parole.significato: Synonym of zongzi (“A traditional Chinese dumpling of glutinous rice stuffed with a savoury or sweet filling, wrapped i…
parole.testo: Borrowed from Hokkien 肉粽 (bah-chàng).

parole.significato: A noodle dish made with minced meat (usually pork), soy sauce, oyster sauce and black vinegar.
parole.testo: From Hokkien 肉脞麵 /肉脞面 (bah-chhò͘-mī).

parole.significato: A Chinese salty-sweet dried meat product similar to jerky.
parole.testo: Borrowed from Hokkien 肉乾 /肉干 (bah-koaⁿ, “dried meat”).

parole.significato: To inform on someone behind his or her back.
parole.testo: From Hokkien 包刀 (pau to, literally “wrapped knife”), referring to backstabbing.

parole.significato: Rice vermicelli, rice noodles.
parole.testo: From Hokkien 米粉 (bí-hún). Doublet of mei fun. Compare Malay bihun, Indonesian bihun, Tagalog bihon.

parole.significato: One's penis.
parole.testo: Reduplication of bird, a semantic loan from Hokkien 鳥 /鸟 (as in 𡳞鳥 /𡳞鸟 and 咕咕鳥 /咕咕鸟) and Malay burung (“bird; penis”). Compare bird, which is also used to refer to the male genitalia in certain North American slang.

parole.significato: black bean; black soybean
parole.testo: From black + Spanish mongo, which is a calque of Hokkien 烏豆 /乌豆 (o͘-tāu, literally “black bean”). See also Tagalog utaw (“black mongo”), Cebuano utaw (“black mongo”).

parole.significato: Final interrogative particle, used to invite agreement.
parole.testo: From Hokkien 無 /无 (bô).

parole.significato: Indifferent, not caring about something, unbothered.
parole.testo: From Hokkien 無插／无插 (bô-chhap, “indifferent; to not care about”).

parole.significato: To leave someone out from an event or activity by not inviting them.
parole.testo: From Hokkien 無／无 (bô, “not”) + 招 (chio, “invite”).

parole.significato: Boring.
parole.testo: From Hokkien 無聊／无聊 (bô-liâu, “bored; boring”).

parole.significato: No choice; it cannot be helped; there’s no other way.
parole.testo: From Hokkien 無變／无变 (bô-piàn, “no choice”).

parole.significato: Impossible
parole.testo: Borrowed from Hokkien 無可能 /无可能 (bô-khó-lêng) in Malaysia and Singapore.

parole.significato: A black tea from Fujian, China.
parole.testo: Borrowed from Hokkien 武夷 (Bú-î) or 武夷茶 (Bú-î-tê, “Bohea tea”), named after the Bohea Hills or in Hokkien 武夷山 (Bú-î-soaⁿ), also known as Wuyi Mountains from Mandarin 武夷山 (Wǔyíshān), in Fujian where the tea is grown. Compare French bou.

parole.significato: Soft drink.
parole.testo: Borrowed from Singaporean Hokkien 沐水 (bok-chúi).

parole.significato: Synonym of bo pian (“no choice; there’s no other way”).
parole.testo: Clipping of bo pian + -s (hypocoristic suffix), from Hokkien 無變／无变 (bô-piàn, “no choice”).

parole.significato: Unhappy
parole.testo: From Hokkien 𣍐爽 /𫧃爽 (bōe-sóng, “unhappy”).

parole.significato: Unable to deal or to handle something or someone; unable to put up with a situation or person much longer.

parole.significato: Economy rice (rice sold with a combination of other dishes).
parole.testo: From Hokkien 菜飯 /菜饭 (chhài-pn̄g).

parole.significato: A sweet cake, often iced, containing grated carrot.

parole.significato: To fail to understand something; be unable to comprehend what others are saying.
parole.testo: Calque of Hokkien 掠無球 /掠无球 (lia̍h bô kiû, “to not understand”, literally “catch no ball”).

parole.significato: Expression of contempt or frustration.

parole.significato: Burnt and charred (e.g., from overcooking).

parole.significato: mixed vegetables

parole.significato: A ten-storey housing flat built by the Singapore Housing and Development Board (HDB) in the 1960s (now mostly vacated).
parole.testo: Borrowed from Hokkien 十樓厝 (cha̍p-lâu-chhù, “ten-storey house”). Originating in the 1960s, with the building of pioneering HDB satellite flats.

parole.significato: Vagina, cunt.

parole.significato: A dirty old man; a pervert.

parole.significato: Synonym of ching bo leung (“type of cold dessert soup”).

parole.significato: To rush or charge, usually to do, complete or obtain something, or to get to a particular place.
parole.testo: From Hokkien 衝／冲 (chhiong, “to rush or charge”).

parole.significato: To inconvenience or disturb; to make a fuss and bother; to act up.

parole.significato: Preserved radish in Asian cuisine.

parole.significato: A bribe or gratuity for a service or for arranging a deal; squeeze.
parole.testo: From Hokkien 感謝 /感谢 (kám-siā, “thanks”).

parole.significato: A Chinese Filipino snack food consisting of a slice of asado/char siu meat and other condiments sandwiched between flat…

parole.significato: A gratuity or tip as thanks for a service
parole.testo: Borrowed from Hokkien 感謝 /感谢 (kám-siā, “thank you”).

parole.significato: Undiluted; with no extra water added to dilute it, making it thicker than kopi gau.
parole.testo: From Hokkien 直落 (ti̍t-lo̍h, “directly from the jug; to pour straight into the cup”, literally “straight down”).

parole.significato: Be quiet.
parole.testo: Unadapted borrowing from Malay diam. For some Chinese speakers, this word is reanalysed as a loan from Hokkien 恬 (tiām, “silent”) or Teochew 恬 (diam⁷, “silent”).

parole.significato: Used to suggest that one is doomed, or as good as dead.
parole.testo: die + liao (indicates a change of state), from Hokkien 了 (liáu) or Teochew 了 (liao²), with the tone of Mandarin 了 (liǎo). Partial calque of Hokkien 死了 (sí liáu).

parole.significato: Synonym of oyster omelette.

parole.significato: Greedy and always on the lookout for cheap deals and freebies.

parole.significato: Any plant of two species of the genus Panax (Panax ginseng and Panax quinquefolius), having forked roots supposed to ha…
parole.testo: Borrowed from Hokkien 人參 /人参 (jîn-sim, “ginseng”). Doublet of ninzin.

parole.significato: Synonym of mongo (“mung bean”).
parole.testo: From green + Spanish mongo, which is a calque of Hokkien 綠豆 /绿豆 (lia̍k-tāu, literally “green bean”).

parole.significato: Hard to please or satisfy; irritating, loathsome.
parole.testo: Derived from Hokkien 怪𡳞 (koài-lān, literally “strange dick”).

parole.significato: maternal grandfather; maternal grandpa.
parole.testo: From Hokkien 外公 (gōa-kong, “maternal grandfather”). Compare Tagalog guwakong.

parole.significato: maternal grandmother; maternal grandma
parole.testo: From Hokkien 外媽 /外妈 (gōa-má, “maternal grandmother”). Compare Tagalog guwama.

parole.significato: beef belly (either ox tripe, tenderloin, or offal) and noodles soup (usually tangy/savory and spicy) with beef shanks o…
parole.testo: Borrowed from Hokkien 牛腩麵 /牛腩面 (gû-lám mī, “beef belly noodles”).

parole.significato: Synonym of ah (sense 1); used to form tag questions prompting the listener to confirm something.
parole.testo: Borrowed from Hokkien 哈 (hâⁿ).

parole.significato: An exclamation of exasperation, said especially when a bad event occurs.
parole.testo: From Hokkien 害矣 (hāi--ah).

parole.significato: pseudojournalists, not employed by a reputable news organization but who pass themselves off as journalists in order to…
parole.testo: From Hokkien 嘐潲 (hau-siâu, “fake”). Compare Tagalog hawsiyaw.

parole.significato: a person who traces his/her ancestry to Putian or the surrounding region

parole.significato: hot and spicy.
parole.testo: Borrowed from Hokkien 薟／莶 (hiam, “spicy”).

parole.significato: Superficial; incompetent or having no substance despite appearances, skin-deep; portraying oneself as greater than one…
parole.testo: From Hokkien 好看無好食 /好看无好食 (hó-khòaⁿ bô hó-chia̍h, literally “good to look at, not good to eat”).

parole.significato: of or relating to Fuqing Eastern Min
parole.testo: From Hokkien 福清 (Hok-chhiaⁿ).

parole.significato: A group of Han Chinese people whose traditional ancestral homes are in southern Fujian, South China, especially those t…
parole.testo: Borrowed from Hokkien 福建 (Hok-kiàn, “Fujian / Fukien”). Doublet of Fukien and Fujian.

parole.significato: A typical Hokkien noodle dish
parole.testo: From Hokkien 福建麵 /福建面 (Hok-kiàn-mī). See also pancit langlang.

parole.significato: To be fucked, to be screwed.
parole.testo: From Hokkien 仾姦 /仾奸 (hōng-kàn, “to get fucked”).

parole.significato: A unit of weight (about 0.378125 of a gram, or 0.0133 of an ounce) used to measure opium in British-controlled parts of…
parole.testo: Borrowed from Hokkien 分 (hun). Doublet of fen and fan.

parole.significato: Used with directives and statements to assert that something should be kept in mind or taken note of.
parole.testo: From Hokkien 乎 (--hohⁿ / --hôⁿ, mood particle) and Cantonese 嗬 (ho², interrogative particle).

parole.significato: To have unexpectedly lost one's way and gone off course; to get lost and end up in some faraway place.
parole.testo: Pronunciation spelling of Hokkien 荷蘭／荷兰 (Hô-lân) and Cantonese 荷蘭／荷兰 (ho⁴ laan⁴⁻¹, “the Netherlands”), itself from Dutch Holland. Analyzable as a shortening of the alternative expression go hor lan or go Holland, literally “to go to Holland; to end up in Holland”.

parole.significato: A traditional, festive expression used to wish oneself prosperity.
parole.testo: From Hokkien 發啊 /发啊 (hoat--a), from 發 /发 (hoat, “to produce, to grow, to develop, to prosper, to pay out”) + 啊 (--a, “particle of exhortation”).

parole.significato: Synonym of see hum (“blood cockles, ark clams”).
parole.testo: Borrowed from Hokkien 蚶 (ham).

parole.significato: Used to draw attention to something one has to say.
parole.testo: From Etymology 1, or a calque of Hokkien 我共汝講 /我共汝讲 (oá kā lí kóng, “let me tell you something; listen up”).

parole.significato: An instant noodle soup dish that is popular in the Philippines and abroad, consisting of pre-cooked noodles with a pack…
parole.testo: From instant + mami, the latter from Hokkien 肉麵 /肉面 (mah-mī).

parole.significato: Of a person, to be westernized; to have abandoned one's own cultural traditions in favor of a westernized lifestyle.
parole.testo: From Malaysian and Singaporean Hokkien 食kentang or 食蕳砃 /食𫈉砃 (chia̍h kan-tang), from 食 (chia̍h, “to eat”) + Malay kentang (“potatoes”). Historically, the choice of potatoes over rice as a staple food, or its inclusion in one’s diet was seen as a shift towards a more Westernized lifestyle.

parole.significato: Sapping one’s strength; tiresome.
parole.testo: Borrowed from Hokkien 食力 (chia̍h-la̍t, “to be exhausting”), with spelling influenced by Mandarin Pinyin.

parole.significato: To invite (someone) to an event or activity.
parole.testo: From Hokkien 招 (chio, “invite”).

parole.significato: An illegal numbers game lottery, using a tambiolo/tambola/tómbola container that is spun or a receptacle, sometimes sha…
parole.testo: Ultimately derived from Hokkien, via Philippine Spanish jueteng, where the use of ⟨j⟩ represents /h/ as it is spelled from Spanish orthography during the Spanish Colonial Era in the Philippines. See more at Tagalog huweteng.

parole.significato: matchmaking; a romantic arrangement to set up a date between two people
parole.testo: Borrowed from Hokkien 介紹 /介绍 (kài-siāu, “to introduce; to recommend”).

parole.significato: Fuck your mother; fuck.
parole.testo: From Hokkien 姦恁娘 /奸恁娘 (kàn-lín-niâ / kàn-ní-nâ).

parole.significato: Fuck your mother; fuck.
parole.testo: From Hokkien 姦恁娘母 /奸恁娘母 (kàn-lín-niâ-bú / kàn-ní-nâ-bú). The variant kan ni na beh likely results from a shortening of the last two syllables in 姦恁娘母的 /奸恁娘母的 (kàn-lín-niâ-bú-ê, “fuck your mother's”) from bú-ê to bé.

parole.parola: kan ni na bu chao chee bye
parole.significato: Extreme expression of anger or frustration.
parole.testo: Combination of kan ni na bu + chao chee bye, from Hokkien 姦恁娘母臭膣屄 /奸恁娘母臭膣屄 (“fuck your mother's stinking cunt”).

parole.significato: To make a fuss, to complain or whine excessively, to complain to high heaven.
parole.testo: From Hokkien 哭爸哭母 (khàu-pē-khàu-bú, “to complain to high heaven”, literally “to quarrel with one’s parents; to weep for one’s father and mother”).

parole.significato: Gaojia opera (a type of Chinese opera originating in Quanzhou, Fujian)
parole.testo: From Hokkien 高甲 (Káu-kah).

parole.significato: To confront.
parole.testo: From Hokkien 哭爸 (khàu-pē, “to cry as if one has lost their father”).

parole.significato: Being a busybody, prying into the business of others.
parole.testo: Borrowed from Hokkien 家婆 (ke-pô).

parole.significato: Alkaline zongzi (a Chinese dessert, sometimes filled with a sweet paste)
parole.testo: From Hokkien 鹼粽 /碱粽 (kiⁿ-chàng).

parole.significato: Mad, crazy.
parole.testo: From Hokkien 起痟 (khí-siáu, “to go mad”).

parole.significato: a Hakka person
parole.testo: From Hokkien 客 (Kheh, literally “guest people”).

parole.significato: Salted vegetables.
parole.testo: From Hokkien 鹹菜 /咸菜 (kiâm-chhài).

parole.significato: salted / pickled Chinese mustard greens (Brassica juncea)
parole.testo: From Hokkien 鹹菜 /咸菜 (kiâm-chhài, literally “salted vegetable”).

parole.significato: A snack made from salted dried plums.
parole.testo: From Hokkien 鹹梅 /咸梅 (kiâm-muî).

parole.significato: Tongs, clip; any claw-like tool used to grab objects or hold something in place.
parole.testo: Borrowed from Hokkien 夾 /夹 (kiap).

parole.significato: Unwilling to take a risk for fear that something bad or unfavorable will happen; cowardly, overly cautious and risk-ave…
parole.testo: Borrowed from Hokkien 驚死／惊死 (kiaⁿ-sí, “afraid to die”).

parole.significato: The quality of being kiasi, a stereotypically Singaporean attitude associated with being overly wary and willing to tak…
parole.testo: kiasi + -ness, from Hokkien 驚死／惊死 (kiaⁿ-sí, “afraid to die”)

parole.significato: Afraid to lose out, particularly because one is overly competitive.
parole.testo: Borrowed from Hokkien 驚輸／惊输 (kiaⁿ-su, “afraid to lose out”).

parole.significato: The mindset associated with being kiasu (overly competitive and afraid to lose out).
parole.testo: kiasu + -ism, from Hokkien 驚輸／惊输 (kiaⁿ-su, “afraid to lose out”)

parole.significato: The quality of being kiasu (overly competitive and afraid to lose out).
parole.testo: kiasu + -ness, from Hokkien 驚輸／惊输 (kiaⁿ-su, “afraid to lose out”)

parole.significato: a small hybrid variety of citrus fruit, similar to a small ponkan, clementine, tangerine, mandarin orange, orange, etc.
parole.testo: Borrowed from Hokkien. See Hokkien 結結 /结结 (kiat-kiat, “to combine; to fuse; to bear (fruit)”), 桔/橘 (kiat) as in 桔仔/橘仔 (kiat-á, “tangerine; mandarin orange”), 傑傑 /杰杰 (kia̍t-kia̍t, “outstanding; remarkable; clever”), 結果 /结果 (kiat-kó, “to bear fruit”), etc.

parole.significato: Chinese celery ("varieties of Apium graveolens, sometimes called Apium graveolens var. secalinum")
parole.testo: Borrowed from Hokkien 芹菜 (khîn-chhài, “celery”).

parole.significato: Happy Chinese New Year
parole.testo: From Hokkien 恭喜發財 /恭喜发财 (Kiong-hí hoat-châi). Compare Tagalog Kiong Hee Huat Tsai.

parole.significato: A benevolent organization of popular origin found among overseas Chinese communities for individuals with the same surn…
parole.testo: Borrowed from Hokkien 公司 (kong-si, “company”). See also Hokkien 公班衙 (kong-pan-gêe / kong-pan-gê), English British East India Company, Dutch Verenigde Oostindische Compagnie (“Dutch East India Company”, literally “United East India Company”).

parole.significato: Term of address for a paternal aunt within some Chinese families.
parole.testo: From Hokkien 姑姑 (ko͘-ko͘, “paternal aunt”).

parole.significato: Penis
parole.testo: Partial calque of Hokkien 咕咕鳥 /咕咕鸟 (ku-kú-chiáu). Compare cuckoo.

parole.significato: Penis, a dick
parole.testo: From Hokkien 咕咕鳥 /咕咕鸟 (ku-kú-chiáu). See also cuckoo bird.

parole.significato: garlic chives; Chinese chives (Allium tuberosum)
parole.testo: Borrowed from Hokkien 韭菜 (kú-chhài, “garlic chives”).

parole.significato: A small, bite-sized dish consisting of a thin, fried pastry tart shell that is shaped like a fluted cup and filled with…
parole.testo: From Hokkien 粿 (kóe, “rice cake”) and English patty (in the sense of patty shell and patty iron). Attested in 1956 as kwei patti cooked with a patti iron in Susie Hing's cookbook In a Malayan Kitchen.

parole.significato: Venus clams (as food)
parole.testo: From Hokkien 啦啦 (la-la), a reduplication of 蜊 (lâ, “clam”).

parole.significato: a stew of cattle genitals
parole.testo: Borrowed from Hokkien 𡳞鳥 /𡳞鸟 (lǎn-chiáu, “penis”). Compare Cebuano lansyaw. Doublet of lanjiao.

parole.significato: Penis
parole.testo: From Hokkien 𡳞鳥 /𡳞鸟 (lān-chiáu). Compare Cebuano lansyaw. Doublet of lanciao. Spelling influenced by Hanyu Pinyin.

parole.significato: To go stale or turn soft from exposure to air.
parole.testo: From Hokkien 漏風 /漏风 (lāu-hong).

parole.significato: To have diarrhoea.
parole.testo: From Hokkien 落屎 (làu-sái).

parole.significato: Lousy; useless; worthless.
parole.testo: From Hokkien 老爺／老爷 (lāu-iâ, “old-fashioned”).

parole.significato: Embarrassing, shameful
parole.testo: Borrowed from Hokkien 落氣 /落气 (làu-khùi, “to lose face”).

parole.significato: A special Chinese banquet with many courses and dishes (especially as served in the Philippines).
parole.testo: Ultimately from Philippine Hokkien 鬧熱 /闹热 (lāu-lia̍t, “bustling; filled with activity”), with semantic shift and slight phonological change due to /l/~/ɾ/ allophony in Hokkien.

parole.significato: Used to convey uncertainty (in response to inconsistent information).
parole.testo: From Hokkien 咧 (--leh, “declarative particle used for emphasis; interrogative particle used to express doubt”).

parole.significato: Indicates action completion, or more generally, perfective aspect.
parole.testo: Borrowed from Hokkien 了 (liáu) and Teochew 了 (liao²), with tone and spelling influenced by Mandarin 了 (liǎo) and its romanization in Hanyu Pinyin.

parole.significato: A reference to oneself in the third person, taking on the stance of a superior. Literally, "your father".
parole.testo: Borrowed from Hokkien 恁爸／林北 (lín-pē, “I; me”, literally “your father”), specifically Singapore Hokkien 恁爸 (lím-pē, “I; me”, literally “your father”).

parole.significato: Sentence-final particle denoting finality or completion.
parole.testo: Borrowed from Hokkien 囉 /啰 (--lo͘). Doublet of lor.

parole.significato: doctor; physician
parole.testo: From Hokkien 老君 (ló-kun), from Malay dukun (“shaman or medicine man”). Doublet of dukun.

parole.significato: A Chinese dish of braised duck in soy sauce.
parole.testo: From Hokkien 滷鴨 /卤鸭 (ló͘-ah).

parole.significato: Long-winded, naggy.
parole.testo: From Hokkien 囉嗦 /啰嗦 (lô-so) or Cantonese 囉嗦 /啰嗦 (lo¹ so¹).

parole.significato: zongzi
parole.testo: Borrowed from Hokkien 肉粽 (mah-chàng).

parole.significato: A traditional Chinese rice cake snack made of glutinous rice, peanuts, and sugar.
parole.testo: From Hokkien 麻糍 (môa-chî).

parole.significato: Do not hesitate; take action immediately.
parole.testo: From Hokkien 莫躇了 (mài thû liáu, “don't hesitate”).

parole.significato: Chinese Filipino thick soup of pork tenderloin, without noodles
parole.testo: From Hokkien 肉羹 (mah-kiⁿ).

parole.significato: Chinese Filipino thick soup of pork tenderloin, with noodles
parole.testo: Borrowed from Hokkien 肉羹麵 /肉羹面 (mah-kiⁿ mī).

parole.significato: Chinese-style wheat noodles.
parole.testo: Borrowed from Hokkien 麵／面 (mī).

parole.significato: A thick, sweet pancake originated in Quanzhou, Fujian, usually with a filling of peanut, coconut or red bean.
parole.testo: From Hokkien 麵煎粿／面煎粿 (mī-chian-kóe), from 麵／面 (mī, “wheat flour”) + 煎 (chian, “pan fried”) + 粿 (kóe, “rice cake, pastry-like snack”).

parole.significato: fried noodles
parole.testo: From mee + Malay goreng, with mee from Hokkien 麵 /面 (mī).

parole.significato: flour for making noodles (such as rice flour; uncooked rice vermicelli noodles)
parole.testo: From Hokkien 麵粉 /面粉 (mī-hún).

parole.significato: Misua; a very thin variety of salted Chinese noodles made from wheat flour.
parole.testo: From Hokkien 麵線 /面线 (mī-soàⁿ). Compare Malay misoa, Indonesian misoa, Tagalog miswa.

parole.significato: Misua; a very thin variety of salted Chinese noodles made from wheat flour.
parole.testo: From Hokkien 麵線 /面线 (mī-soàⁿ). Compare Tagalog miswa, Malay misoa, Indonesian misoa.

parole.significato: A traditional snack made of glutinous rice, usually mixed with crushed peanuts and sugar.
parole.testo: From Hokkien 麻糍 (môa-chî, “glutinous rice cake made with hemp-seeds”), from 麻 (môa, “hemp”) + 糍 (chî, “glutinous rice cake”).

parole.significato: Stingy, miserly
parole.testo: From Hokkien 貓 /猫 (niau / ngiau, “cat; stingy”), with influence from Singapore Teochew 貓 /猫 (ngiao¹, “cat; stingy”). See also Hokkien 貓潲 /猫潲 (niau-siâu, “stingy”), 貓神 /猫神 (niau-sîn, “stingy”), 貓𡳞 /猫𡳞 (niau-lān / niau-lǎn, “stingy”), 貓筩 /猫筒 (niau-thāng, “stingy”).

parole.significato: Only, merely, that's all; used at the end of a sentence to emphasize that something is trivial, small or undemanding.
parole.testo: From Hokkien 爾／尔 (niā, “only”).

parole.significato: Exceptionally good
parole.testo: Calque of Hokkien 無馬走 /无马走 (bô-bé-cháu, literally “no horse can outrun”), originally used within the context of horse racing to describe a competitor far ahead in the field.

parole.significato: A variant of bak chang (zongzi) originating in Peranakan cuisine, made with minced pork, candied winter melons and some…
parole.testo: Borrowed from Hokkien 娘惹粽 (niô͘-nia-chàng). Analysable as Nyonya (from Malay nyonya) + Hokkien 粽 (“rice dumpling wrapped in leaves”).

parole.significato: With sugar and no condensed milk added.
parole.testo: From Hokkien 烏 /乌 (o͘, “black”) or Teochew 烏 /乌 (ou¹, “black”).

parole.significato: Used at the end of a sentence to highlight the characteristics of someone or something.
parole.testo: Analogous to several senses of Hokkien 個／个 (ê) and Mandarin 的 (de, declarative particle, nominalizer, etc.). This semantic loan might have stemmed from the apparent similarity between one as a prop-word and 的 (de) or 個 /个 (ê) as a nominalizer (e.g. 青色的 (“the green one”)). Compare Cantonese 嘅 (ge³).

parole.significato: A type of tea with a taste in between green tea and black tea.
parole.testo: Either a partial calque of Mandarin 烏龍茶 /乌龙茶 (wūlóngchá), or directly from Hokkien 烏龍茶 /乌龙茶 (o͘-liông-tê), from 烏龍 /乌龙 (o͘-liông, literally “black dragon”) + 茶 (tê, “tea”).

parole.significato: Final interrogative particle, forming a yes/no question from a declarative statement.
parole.testo: Calque of Hokkien 抑無 /抑无 (a̍h-bô / á-bô, literally “or not; or no; or none”). See also Hokkien 是毋是 (sī-m̄-sī / sǐ-m̄-sǐ, “whether or not”), 是抑毋是 (sī á-m̄-sī / sǐ á-m̄-sǐ, “isn't?”, literally “is it? or is it not?”), Mandarin 是不是 (shìbùshì, “whether or not”), forming a question, and similar interroga

parole.significato: An interjection expressing disapproval, used to tease someone who has done something wrong, subsequently getting themse…
parole.testo: Possibly from Hokkien 嗚呼 /呜呼 (o͘-ho͘, “used to express condolences in funeral orations; (euphemistic) to die, to pass away”).

parole.significato: Of a man: to masturbate.
parole.testo: From Hokkien 拍手銃 /拍手铳 (phah-chhiú-chhèng, literally “to shoot or fire one’s gun”).

parole.significato: gangster; hooligan
parole.testo: Borrowed from Hokkien 歹囝 (pháiⁿ-kiáⁿ).

parole.significato: Embarrassed; humiliated; shy
parole.testo: From Hokkien 歹勢／歹势 (phái-sè, “embarrassed”).

parole.significato: mami (A traditional Filipino noodle soup made with egg noodles and usually including a variety of ingredients such as c…
parole.testo: From pancit + mami, both ultimately from Hokkien.

parole.significato: To urinate; to pee.
parole.testo: Borrowed from Hokkien 放尿 (pàng-jiō).

parole.significato: To defecate; to shit.
parole.testo: Borrowed from Hokkien 放屎 (pàng-sái).

parole.significato: To deliberately miss an agreed appointment, especially at the last minute.
parole.testo: Hokkien 放生 (pàng seⁿ) to release, to set free.

parole.significato: the Chinese cabbage (either napa cabbage or bok choy)
parole.testo: From Hokkien 白菜 (pe̍h-chhài, “Chinese cabbage”, literally “white vegetable”). Doublet of bok choy.

parole.significato: Frustrated, exasperated, fed up.
parole.testo: From Hokkien 迫促 (pek-chhek).

parole.significato: A high-quality black tea made using young leaves, grown in Sri Lanka, India, Java and the Azores.
parole.testo: Unclear; possibly from Hokkien 白毫 (pe̍h-ho, “white hair”) or Hokkien 白花 (pe̍h-hoe, “white flower”). See Tea leaf grading#Etymology. Compare to Russian ба́йховый (bájxovyj).

parole.significato: Iced; with ice added.
parole.testo: From Hokkien 冰 (peng, “ice”).

parole.significato: Chinese cabbage (either napa cabbage or bok choy)
parole.testo: Borrowed from Hokkien 白菜 (pe̍h-chhài). Doublet of pechay and bok choy.

parole.significato: Thinner; with more water added to dilute it.
parole.testo: From Hokkien 薄 (po̍h / po̍k, “weak”).

parole.significato: Chinese spinach
parole.testo: From Hokkien 菠倫菜 /菠伦菜 (po͘-lûn-chhài, “spinach”).

parole.significato: Interjection expressing strong disdain.
parole.testo: From Hokkien 呸 (phùi, “to spit”), itself onomatopoeic.

parole.significato: red bean; azuki bean
parole.testo: From red + Spanish mongo, which is a calque of Hokkien 紅豆 /红豆 (âng-tāu, literally “red bean”).

parole.significato: A small, sweet, round Chinese dumpling with sticky glutinous rice flour skin wrapped around a sweet filling, moulded to…
parole.testo: Calque of Hokkien 紅龜粿 /红龟粿 (âng-ku-kóe, literally “red tortoise cake”).

parole.significato: A toxic crystalline substance obtained from the roots of derris and related plants, widely used as an insecticide.
parole.testo: From Japanese ローテン (rōten) + -one (“ketone”), from Hokkien 蘆藤 /芦藤 (lôo-tîn, “Derris elliptica”).

parole.significato: Shit
parole.testo: Borrowed from Hokkien 屎 (sái, “shit”).

parole.significato: Someone who is always assigned or forced to do unpleasant tasks.
parole.testo: From Hokkien 屎工 (sái-kang, “undesirable, menial tasks”, literally “shit jobs”) + warrior.

parole.significato: Drunk or inebriated, or appearing so; tipsy.
parole.testo: From Hokkien or Teochew. Its exact origins are unclear, possible etymologies include: * Hokkien 逝 (sē, “to pass away”), which may have been used as a hyperbole to describe someone who has passed out. * Hokkien 垂垂 (sê-sê, “(literary) to droop, to hang low”). * Clipping of Taiwanese Hokkien 馬西／马西 (má-

parole.significato: the youngest sister
parole.testo: Borrowed from Hokkien 小妹 (sió-bē, “younger sister; youngest sister”).

parole.significato: the youngest brother
parole.testo: Borrowed from Hokkien 小弟 (sió-tǐ, “younger brother; youngest brother”).

parole.significato: Synonym of die liao.
parole.testo: Borrowed from Hokkien 死了 (sí liáu).

parole.significato: Causing embarrassment or disgrace to others.
parole.testo: From Hokkien 瀉衰／泻衰 (sià-soe), 卸衰 (sià-sue).

parole.significato: To move aside; to get out of the way.
parole.testo: From Hokkien 閃 /闪 (siám, “to dodge”).

parole.significato: Bored, weary or fed up; tired (of something).
parole.testo: From Hokkien 𤺪 (siān).

parole.significato: Mad; crazy
parole.testo: From Hokkien 痟 (siáu, “mad; crazy”).

parole.significato: An intensifier word, very.
parole.testo: From Singapore Hokkien 死爸 (sí-pē, “very; quite”, literally “die father”), from Singapore Teochew 死爸 (si² bê⁶, “very; quite”, literally “die father”), in the sense of being to the extent that one’s father dies.

parole.significato: An expression of disbelief, equivalent to Is it so?
parole.testo: Derived from Hokkien 是無／是无 (sī-bô, “is not”).

parole.significato: What?; what is this […] ?; what […] are you talking about?
parole.testo: From Hokkien 什物 or 什麼／什么 (sím-mi̍h, “what”).

parole.significato: A traditional Chinese physician.
parole.testo: From Hokkien 先生 (sin-seⁿ). Doublet of sensei, from Japanese 先生(せんせい) (sensei).

parole.significato: A traditional steamed Chinese pork dumpling served as part of the dim sum menu.
parole.testo: Borrowed from Hokkien 燒賣 /烧卖 (sio-mai, sio-māi), from Cantonese 燒賣 /烧卖 (siu¹ maai⁶⁻²). Doublet of shumai and siew mai.

parole.significato: Very tough, challenging.
parole.testo: From Hokkien 傷 /伤 (siong).

parole.significato: Chinese steamed stuffed bun; baozi (usually char siu bao, especially the Philippine variant known as "siopao asado")
parole.testo: From Philippine Hokkien 燒包 /烧包 (sio-pau), itself from Cantonese 叉燒包 /叉烧包 (caa¹ siu¹ baau¹). See also siomai.

parole.significato: Calm; self-assured.
parole.testo: Singapore English steady (“solid, cool-headed, reliable”) + Hokkien 歕觱觱 /𬅫觱觱 (pûn pi-pi, “to blow a whistle”, onomatopoeic).

parole.significato: greasyback shrimp; sand shrimp (Metapenaeus ensis)
parole.testo: Borrowed from Hokkien 沙蝦 /沙虾 (soa-hê, literally “sand shrimp”). Compare Tagalog suwahe.

parole.significato: Someone who is uneducated; a country bumpkin.
parole.testo: From Hokkien 山龜／山龟 (soaⁿ-ku, “mountain turtle”), from 山 (soaⁿ, “mountain”) + 龜／龟 (ku, “turtle”).

parole.significato: unlucky, unfortunate
parole.testo: Borrowed from Hokkien 衰 (soe).

parole.significato: Great, neat, nice, excellent (often used as an interjection when something has gone smoothly).
parole.testo: From Hokkien 媠 (súi, “pretty”). Compare Tagalog yasuwi. Perhaps reinforced by sweet.

parole.significato: One's business or responsibility. More often than not, used in a dismissive manner.
parole.testo: From Hokkien 代誌 /代志 (tāi-chì, “affair, matter, (abstract) thing”).

parole.significato: To talk nonsense.
parole.testo: Either a calque of Hokkien 講𡳞鳥話 /讲𡳞鸟话 (kóng lān-chiáu-ōe), from 講話／讲话 (kóng-ōe, “talk”) + 𡳞鳥／𡳞鸟 (lān-chiáu, “cock (penis)”), or influenced by the English phrase cock-and-bull story.

parole.significato: boss; owner (of a business entity such as shop, etc.); shop owner; shopkeeper; business owner; employer (especially a C…
parole.testo: Borrowed from Hokkien 頭家 /头家 (thâu-ke, “boss”). Doublet of towkay. Compare Tagalog taoke, Tausug tawki, Malay tauke, Indonesian tauke, Burmese ထောင်ကဲ (htaungkai:), Puyuma tawki, Rukai tawki, Sakizaya tawki.

parole.significato: Mung bean sprouts.
parole.testo: From Hokkien 豆芽 (tāu-gê).

parole.significato: a mainlander from mainland China; mainland Chinese (to differentiate from a Chinese Filipino raised in the Philippines…
parole.testo: Initialism of Philippine Hokkien 大陸仔 /大陆仔 (tāi-lio̍k-á, “mainlander”), which is often perceived as "Tai Diok Ka" or "Tai Diok A", due to /l~d/ allophony usually preceding an /i/ vowel and the concept of forming initialisms from the consonant-sounding phonemes that syllables seemingly sound like they

parole.significato: Synonym of cheeko pek; dirty old man.
parole.testo: From Hokkien 猪哥伯 (ti-ko peh, “dirty old man; lecherous and licentious man”, literally “uncle boar”).

parole.significato: Correct; that's right.
parole.testo: Borrowed from Hokkien 著 (tio̍h).

parole.significato: Right?, is that right? (checking agreement or seeking confirmation)
parole.testo: Borrowed from Hokkien 著無 /著无 (tio̍h bô, “right?”, literally “correct no?”).

parole.significato: Synonym of SOHCAHTOA.
parole.testo: Inversion of SOH-CAH-TOA, nearly homophonic with Hokkien 大跤嫂 (tōa-kha-só, literally “middle-aged woman with huge feet”).

parole.significato: To collapse (fail or break down internally); to fall asleep or collapse from exhaustion.
parole.testo: From Hokkien 倒 (tó, “to fall down, to collapse, to go bankrupt”).

parole.significato: A business owner; boss (especially a Chinese Malaysian or Chinese Singaporean boss).
parole.testo: From Hokkien 頭家 /头家 (thâu-ke, “boss”). Doublet of taoke.

parole.significato: A kind of single-masted traditional boat with a junk rig, formerly used on the Singapore River along with the tongkang.
parole.testo: From Hokkien 大䑩 (tōa-ko͘).

parole.significato: About to; indicates imminent action.
parole.testo: Semantic loan from Hokkien 欲 (beh) or 愛 /爱 (ài) and later Mandarin 要 (yào).

parole.significato: Used to challenge the validity of an assertion.
parole.testo: Compare Hokkien 佗落有 (tó-lo̍h ū, “how is it […] ?”, literally “where is there”). 有 (“have; there is”) is rendered as got in Singlish. Also compare Malay mana ada and Mandarin 哪裡有 /哪里有 (nǎlǐ yǒu).

parole.significato: Grudging admission of defeat in an argument.
parole.testo: win + liao (perfective aspect and change of state marker) + lor (final particle used to express resignation), from Hokkien 了 (liâu) and Cantonese 囉 /啰 (lo¹) respectively.

parole.significato: Handsome, pretty boy.
parole.testo: Borrowed from Hokkien 緣投 /缘投 (iân-tâu, “handsome”); spelling influenced by Mandarin's Hanyu Pinyin romanization. Compare Tagalog yantaw.

parole.significato: extremely skilled; talented.
parole.testo: From Hokkien 在 (chāi, “steady”); likely a shortening of Hokkien 在穩 /在稳 (chāi-ún, “experienced and composed; safe; reliable; trustworthy”), in the sense of a person being solid, experienced, and collected under pressure.

parole.significato: To leave hastily, to take off.
parole.testo: From Hokkien 走 (cháu, “to run”), with Pinyin-based spelling.

parole.significato: Lady or woman.
parole.testo: Borrowed from Hokkien 查某 (cha-bó͘, “woman, girl”).

parole.significato: To modify (a gadget or vehicle).
parole.testo: From Hokkien 裝 /装 (chng), compare Cantonese 裝 /装 (zong¹, “to install; to redecorate”). Spelling influenced by Mandarin Pinyin.

parole.significato: Exact, precise, spot-on.
parole.testo: From Hokkien 準 /准 (chún) or Mandarin 準 /准 (zhǔn).

parole.significato: Affordable homestyle or restaurant-style Chinese dishes, from stalls commonly found in hawker centres and coffee shops.
parole.testo: Borrowed from Singaporean Hokkien 煮炒 (chír-chhá, literally “cook and fry”), with Pinyin-influenced spelling.
